A small offset comes from working-capital and Middle East/North America drag. findings.finding: Espressif (688018.SH), the largest Chinese Wi-Fi/BLE IoT SoC vendor and an upstream supplier to the module ecosystem Tuya's PaaS sells into, reported Q3 2026 revenue of RMB 889M, +33.4% YoY. That is an acceleration from +21.1% in Q2 2026. Telink (688591) Q3 revenue was +17.5% YoY. Tuya's bar asks for +13-16% after +16% in Q2. Caveat: Espressif said smart-home demand was only 'relatively stable' and that its growth came from non-smart-home uses, so the read-through to Tuya's smart-home-heavy PaaS is partial.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: revenue $92.9M against $87.8M consensus (a 5.8% beat), and the stock moved -0.56% close to close (https://www.allinvestview.com/earnings/TUYA/q2-2026/). Q1 2026: a narrow EPS miss with shares reported roughly unchanged. Revenue beats have not been paid for.
findings.why_not_priced: The Espressif print is a Shanghai STAR-board filing in Chinese, and the US consensus for Tuya rests on one or two analysts whose Q3 numbers ($93.1M / $95.8M) imply no acceleration over Q2. If the market had priced an upstream IoT acceleration, the stock would not have drifted to a 52-week low, ~20% below its post-Q2 level, with no company news.
findings.independence: Telink Q3 2026 +17.5% YoY (https://news.10jqka.com.cn/20261029/c681245266.shtml) points the same way. Espressif Q2 2026 +21.1% with smart home in single digits (https://quote.cfi.cn/jyzj/93366/688018.html) is the same company at the prior quarter and the source of the smart-home caveat.

findings.finding: China's exports rose 36.3% YoY in September 2026 and 35.2% in October 2026 ($412.3B), with exports to the US +32.9% in October. Tuya's PaaS customers are largely Chinese brands and OEMs making smart devices for export. In Q3 2025, PaaS was hit by the April-2025 tariff shock: total revenue grew only +1.1% that quarter, which makes the Q3 2026 comparison easy.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no clean history of this line moving the stock. Revenue beats bought roughly 0 to +2% (Q2 2026).
findings.why_not_priced: This is a macro series and widely seen, so it is mostly priced into broad China exposure. It enters Tuya only through transmission the company has not confirmed. If it were priced into Tuya specifically, the consensus would sit above Q2's +16% growth rather than at or below it.
findings.independence: This is a proxy and the company has not confirmed it. The Q2 2026 call said demand recovery is 'gradual and uneven', with the Middle East paused and price sensitivity in North America (https://www.mitrade.com/insights/news/live-news/article-0-2028539-20260825), which tempers it. The September figure comes from ITV (https://www.itv.com/news/2026-11-10/chinas-trade-surplus-exceeds-1-trillion-for-a-2nd-straight-year), as relayed in a search summary.

findings.finding: On the Q2 2026 call the CFO said the company had 'passed through the cost raise' on most products and was protecting gross profit dollars rather than gross margin. He also said costs should settle within 'the next 2 quarters or 3'. So Q3 revenue gets an inflation tailwind from higher semiconductor prices. The gross margin is likely to sit at or below Q2's 46.3% (48.4% a year earlier), which the market may read as poorer quality.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Gross margin has fallen YoY in Q1 2026 (46.9% vs 48.5%) and Q2 2026 (46.3% vs 48.4%), and the stock was roughly flat on both prints. Margin compression has not been punished yet.
findings.why_not_priced: This is in the call transcript, so it is partly public. A single-analyst bar that has not been raised above Q2's run-rate suggests the pass-through to revenue is not fully modelled. If it were, the revenue consensus would carry the price uplift on top of volume.
findings.independence: This shares a theme, but not a document, with finding 1: Espressif's margin rose on scale. The memory and component price surge through 2026 is documented at https://www.cnx-software.com/2026/01/29/electronics-components-price-and-lead-time-increases-announced-across-the-board-and-not-only-because-of-ram/.

findings.finding: Working capital: H1 2026 operating cash flow was $12.6M against $34.4M of net income. Q2 operating cash flow was $6.2M, -66% YoY. Inventory doubled from $30.9M to $63.8M over H1, and prepayments rose from $16.5M to $29.2M; the CFO called this an inventory 'buffer' against cost rises. If Q3 cash conversion stays weak, or the inventory carries a provision, that is a quality-of-earnings negative for a stock valued mostly on its cash.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026, the first quarter with the cash-flow drop, moved -0.56%. It was not punished on the day, though the stock fell 6% over the following month (allinvestview).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the stock has slid since August. The Q3 cash walk is new information. A reversal (inventory selling through into the pass-through revenue) would turn this positive, which is why the band is wide on both sides.
findings.independence: The same figures appear in the Q2 2026 release (https://www.placera.se/pressmeddelanden/tuya-reports-second-quarter-2026-unaudited-financial-results-20260825). The CFO's 'buffering on the inventory' remark is in the same call transcript as finding 3, so the two share a document.

findings.finding: Capital return: Tuya paid interim dividends with its Q2 results in August 2024 ($0.0589/share) and August 2025 ($0.054, about $33M), but declared none in August 2026. The 2026-11-09 board-meeting notice for Q3 lists results only. The February 2026 notice had explicitly flagged a proposed dividend. H1 2026 buybacks were only $1.63M, against a general mandate of up to 10% of shares, while the market cap (~$899M) sits below cash (~$976M). A dividend with Q3 is unlikely given the notice. A buyback announcement or step-up on the call is an upside tail, not the base case.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no clean reaction to a capital-return announcement in what I found. The February 2025 print (Q4 2024 results plus a dividend) fell 12.4% intraday on 2025-02-24 (https://www.tipranks.com/news/the-fly/tuya-falls-12-4), but that move was not tied to the dividend.
findings.why_not_priced: The missing August interim dividend is public and probably part of why the stock fell below cash, so the downside of 'no dividend' is largely in the price. A buyback, if announced, is not priced: a stock at 0.92x cash would not sit at a 52-week low if holders expected one.
findings.independence: The August 2026 board notice also omits a dividend (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001829118/000110465926093007/tm2622565d1_ex99-1.htm). The August 2025 dividend is at https://finviz.com/news/150216/tuya-reports-second-quarter-2025-unaudited-financial-results-and-declaration-of-cash-dividend. The H1 2026 buyback and mandate come from an iTiger summary of the interim report (https://www.itiger.com/news/1130204688), which I have not checked against the primary filing.

findings.finding: Regional drag management named for Q3: in August 2026 the CFO said the Middle East business was paused by military conflict, with recovery 'perhaps maybe end of Q3 or Q4'. He also described North American low-priced devices as price-sensitive, and traditional lighting and IP-camera categories as recovering slowly. These hold back Q3 PaaS against the export-series tailwind.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The same commentary on the Q2 2026 call came with a -0.56% reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: it was said on the call and is probably in the single-analyst bar. What is new is whether the Middle East came back by the end of Q3, which the release and call will show.
findings.independence: The same call transcript as finding 3 (one document, read twice on different lines). The Mitrade call summary (https://www.mitrade.com/insights/news/live-news/article-0-2028539-20260825) carries the same points.

rejected_candidates.detail: Cheapness and an unexplained drawdown are not findings in themselves. The below-cash fact is carried inside finding 5 (capital return), which is the only mechanism found that could close the gap inside the window.

rejected_candidates.detail: Already public on 2026-11-12, it has no revenue line in Q3 and the stock fell after it. It adds nothing to the reported-quarter or capital-return findings, so it is folded in as context rather than filed. A panel may judge otherwise.

baseline_tension: The baseline has no skew and no implied move. The 20-day run-up is -11%, to a 52-week low below cash, with a non-crowded short (0.24%, 3.6 days to cover). My small positive lean runs against the price trend, and nothing in the record explains the trend, so p_up is held near 50.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (bar from two single-analyst sources that disagree, $93.1M vs $95.8M): capped the revenue-dependent findings. Espressif read-through cut from +0.8 to +0.5, export series from +0.5 to +0.3.
Rule 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction; the Q2 2026 5.8% revenue beat bought -0.56%): cost pass-through cut from +0.2 to +0.1. p_up cut from 55 to 54.
Rule 9 (segment net of the rest): the Espressif finding now states that its growth was non-smart-home and sizes the read-through to Tuya net of that.
Rule 3 (own caveat reaches the number): capital-return upside cut from +0.3 to +0.2, because the 2026-11-09 board notice is a document arguing against a dividend.
Left standing: the two negatives (working capital and regional drag) at -0.3 each, and abs_move_pct at 4.5, since the core says uncertainty about the sign does not shrink it.
